deviation_from_production: Backtests ONLY the 4 signals computable from historical daily bars (price_vs_20d_low, rsi_14, volume_spike, sector_relative_strength = 55% of production's weight). The other 4 production signals (insider_buying_30d 20%, short_interest_pct 10%, cash_burn_months 10%, news_sentiment 5% = 45% of weight) require point-in-time historical data (insider Form 4 filings, FINRA short interest, fundamentals, news sentiment as-of a past date) that has no historical query API in this codebase's fetchers (openinsider.py, finra.py, finnhub.py, sec_edgar.py are all 'as-of-today' lookups). This is a deliberate, disclosed scope reduction, not a hidden simplification.

universe.source: Live output of models.trading.low_value.scanner.build_low_value_universe(), snapshotted ONCE on the day the backtest is run (via fetch_universe.py), then held FIXED for the entire historical lookback window.
universe.assumption: Membership is NOT re-verified day-by-day across history (would require historical market-cap/bankruptcy/earnings-blackout data this codebase cannot fetch point-in-time). The backtest asks 'how would today's real qualifying universe's price/technical composite have performed historically', not 'how would the full daily-rebuilt scanner have performed'.

data_source: Alpaca CLI (alpaca data bars), feed=iex (free tier, matches fetchers/alpaca.py production convention), adjustment=split
signal_weight_redistribution: Same algorithm as production compute_thesis_score: any of the 4 signals returning None (insufficient warmup history) is excluded and its weight redistributed proportionally across the signals that ARE available that day. A day with zero available signals produces no score (no trade).

sector_etf_mapping.source: thesis_tracker.sector_etf_for_symbol() called ONCE per symbol on the day the backtest is run (live Finnhub industry lookup), then held fixed for the whole window.
sector_etf_mapping.assumption: Sector/industry classification does not change day-to-day, so using today's classification for the whole historical window is treated as immaterial and disclosed rather than re-verified per day.

entry_rule.rationale: Production docstring frames this as a 'buy the fear' contrarian thesis; low_value_runner.py sizing/exit language (target/stop on a single position) is long-only. No short-side execution rule exists anywhere in the production runner, so SELL/STRONG_SELL composite readings are treated as no-trade in this backtest, not shorted.
entry_rule.trigger: composite >= ENTRY_THRESHOLD (40.0), evaluated on bar T's close
entry_rule.fill_model: next_open bar-proxy with 5 bps slippage (no quotes available from daily bars)
entry_rule.position_sizing: models.trading.shared.kelly.low_value_position_size() — fixed $25 notional per trade, fractional shares
entry_rule.entry_priority_when_multiple_signals_sam: Deterministic: symbols sorted alphabetically; fills available slots in that order. Documented as an arbitrary tie-break, not a production behavior (production's single daily runner naturally never sees this tie since it processes sequentially).

exit_rule.deviation_from_production: Production's exit also includes a NEGATIVE_THESES->POSITIVE_CATALYST news-flag resolution path. That path requires historical news data with per-day sentiment/category flags, which is not available for backtesting, so it is OMITTED here. Only the two objective price rules and the time-based rule are modeled.
exit_rule.evaluation_timing: checked against bar T's close (unrealized P&L on the position's average entry price)
exit_rule.intrabar_conflict_policy: N/A at daily granularity beyond fill_model; if both stop and target would be breached within the same historical close-to-close move, the stop is checked first (conservative).

benchmark.fill_model: same next_open convention, single lump-sum entry at the backtest's first available trading day, same initial cash basis as the strategy

fees.rationale: SEC Section 31 fee and FINRA TAF are both charged as a tiny fraction of a cent per $25 notional trade (sub-cent territory) and this sandbox could not fetch/verify current rates from Alpaca's Brokerage Fee Schedule PDF (files.alpaca.markets/disclosures/library/BrokFeeSched.pdf returned 403 to this environment's fetch tool). Fees are excluded and documented as excluded rather than guessed. See fee_source.json (generated at run time) for the disclosure and PDF link required by the backtesting skill.

look_ahead_bias_controls: Signal computed strictly from bars up to and including T's close; never from T+1 or later.
Fills always execute at T+1 open, never at T's own close/open.
Universe/sector-map snapshot is taken on the run date, used only to select which symbols to study and how to map them to a sector ETF — not used as a historical per-day filter.
known_biases_not_controlled: Survivorship bias: universe is snapshotted from TODAY's live scan, so any symbol that would have qualified for Low Value historically but has since been delisted, acquired, or otherwise dropped from today's tradable-asset list is invisible to this backtest.

No walk-forward/out-of-sample split is applied; ENTRY_THRESHOLD, target/stop percentages, and hold-days are production's existing constants, not fit to this backtest window, so overfitting risk here is limited to the fact these constants themselves are still v1/uncalibrated per CLAUDE.md's Low Value section.
